recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-27885 unless Pharmacy wants a separate editorial cleanup of duplicated MedicationRequest narrative.
issue_request: FHIR-27885 was Published/Persuasive for R5 by Pharmacy and requested MedicationRequest guidance explaining when each prescribed drug is a separate MedicationRequest, when shared MedicationRequest.groupIdentifier groups independently managed medication orders, when a parent RequestGroup handles optionality or timing relationships, and that List or Composition should not be used for those grouping requirements.
initial_application: The Jira comments show approved text in July 2020 and a December 2020 note that it had not yet been applied. Commit 1683ac64141af807564d62a28932d70133142fb3 later applied FHIR-27885 by adding the Grouping Medication Requests section to source/medicationrequest/medicationrequest-notes.xml under Dosage Instructions.
additional_context: MedicationRequest is active in source/fhir.ini, placing source/medicationrequest/medicationrequest-notes.xml in current build scope. Later accepted work for FHIR-24619 renamed RequestGroup to RequestOrchestration and commit 46bea37a00e63d1ace04a5f322614c6d0815f500 updated the same guidance accordingly. A 2025 dosage refactor also copied similar grouping guidance into source/medicationrequest/medicationrequest-introduction.xml, and community searches found no conflicting evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active source already contains the requested grouping section and preserves the Jira-approved semantics, with the later RequestOrchestration resource name.

related_jiras.note: Renamed RequestGroup to RequestOrchestration and explains the current resource name in the FHIR-27885 guidance.
